reasons: All three endpoints return hard-coded example results instead of calculations.
The fixed model ID makes different models look identical.
The database session is accepted but never used.

terms.meaning: a web address the app listens on, which runs a specific piece of code
the code attached to an endpoint
stand-in code that returns fixed values until the real logic is written

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Brings in the router, request checking, the database session and the UUID type.
sections.why: Likely reason: every endpoint in this file needs these.
sections.watch_out: The router must be attached to the main app, or these endpoints do not exist.

sections.name: FitModelRequest
sections.title: Fit request shape
sections.what: Describes what a caller sends to fit a model: a project ID, an element name that defaults to total, and a list of feature names.
sections.why: Likely reason: checks input before the logic runs.
sections.watch_out: The default feature list is fixed in code, so callers who skip it get these drivers whether or not they suit the project.

sections.name: FitModelResponse
sections.title: Fit reply shape
sections.what: Describes the reply from a fit: model ID, element, fit score, comparator count and coefficients.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets the fields the caller can expect.
sections.watch_out: Coefficients are an untyped dictionary, so their keys are not checked.

sections.name: VarianceRequest
sections.title: Variance request shape
sections.what: Describes a variance request with a project ID and the model ID to explain.
sections.why: Likely reason: the variance and levers endpoints both need these two IDs.
sections.watch_out: The model ID is not checked against the project ID, so mismatched pairs are accepted.

sections.name: VarianceResponse
sections.title: Variance reply shape
sections.what: Describes the reply with the baseline cost, total variance and a list of steps.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches what a waterfall chart needs.
sections.watch_out: Values are plain numbers, so rounding is left to the caller.

sections.name: LeversResponse
sections.title: Lever reply shape
sections.what: Describes the reply as a list of lever entries.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps lever entries flexible while the format is still being settled.
sections.watch_out: Entries are untyped, so a missing field only shows up later.

sections.name: fit_parametric_model
sections.title: Cost model fit endpoint
sections.what: Accepts a fit request and returns a fixed model with a fit score of 0.85 and 25 comparators, without reading any data.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until the fitting code is written. The docstring describes the intended robust regression.
sections.watch_out: The docstring promises a real fit, but the returned values are constant and would mislead.

sections.name: calculate_variance
sections.title: Variance breakdown endpoint
sections.what: Accepts project and model IDs and returns a fixed baseline, total variance and a four-step waterfall.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until real variance logic exists.
sections.watch_out: The total variance of 300000 does not match the waterfall, which ends back at the baseline, so the numbers contradict each other.

sections.name: generate_optimization_levers
sections.title: Cost-reduction levers endpoint
sections.what: Accepts the same request shape as the variance endpoint and returns two fixed levers with dollar savings, feasibility and constraints.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until real lever generation exists.
sections.watch_out: Lever names and savings are fixed text and numbers, not derived from the project.

summary: Exposes three API endpoints for cost modeling, cost variance and cost-reduction levers, all of which currently return fixed example numbers.
purpose: Lets a front end or other program request a fitted cost model, a variance breakdown and a list of levers for a project.
why: Likely reason: the routes are set up first so the front end can be built against them, with real logic to come. The placeholder comments say so.
how: 1) Each request is checked against its request shape. 2) A database session is provided. 3) The route returns a fixed response. It does not read or write the database.
inputs: Project ID, model ID, element name and feature list.
outputs: Fixed example model, waterfall and lever data.
risks: Every endpoint returns made-up numbers that look real, so they could be reported as results. The fitted model is not saved, and the model ID returned is always the same.
debug: If numbers never change, check whether the route is still a placeholder. If a request is rejected, check that the IDs are valid UUIDs.
